## Berlin Rent Increase Review

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

You have two separate items to verify: the **12% rent increase** and the **3-month notice clause**. I’ll keep this non-legal and focused on what to ask, what to review, and how to request clarification.

## Lease Questions and Key Clauses to Review

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/book.svg

| Topic | What to check | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Rent increase basis | Does the lease allow increases during the fixed term, and under what conditions? | Helps you see whether the landlord is relying on the lease, a statutory rule, or a renewal change. |
| Notice timing | When was the increase notice sent, and by what method? | Timing and delivery can affect whether the request is valid or effective. |
| Effective date | From what date would the higher rent start? | Lets you compare the proposed date with your lease end date of **2026-08-31**. |
| Lease end vs. renewal | Does the lease automatically end, renew, or convert to open-ended tenancy? | Determines whether the landlord is asking for a change before expiration or at renewal. |
| 3-month notice clause | What exactly does the clause say, and what does it apply to? | It may refer to termination, renewal notice, or a different obligation. |
| Rent definition | Is the increase based on cold rent, warm rent, or another rent component? | Avoids confusion about what is actually being increased. |
| Indexation / step-up clause | Is there a CPI, index, or scheduled increase clause already in the lease? | If present, the 12% figure may need to match that clause. |
| Caps or limits | Does the lease mention any limit on increases? | Useful for checking whether the proposed amount fits the contract language. |
| Ancillary costs | Are utilities, service charges, or deposits affected? | A rent increase should not be mixed up with other charges. |
| Written proof | Can the landlord provide the calculation and legal/contract basis in writing? | Gives you a clear record and makes the request easier to review. |

### Checklist of Questions to Ask

- What exact lease clause is the landlord relying on for the **12% increase**?
- Is the increase meant to apply **before** the lease ends on **2026-08-31**, or only for a renewal?
- Does the **3-month notice** clause apply to ending the lease, changing rent, or both?
- When was the notice sent, and can you share a copy of it?
- What is the proposed **effective date** of the new rent?
- Is the increase calculated on **cold rent** or **total monthly rent**?
- Does the lease include any **indexation, step-up, or adjustment clause**?
- Is the landlord asking for a **new agreement**, an **amendment**, or just notice of a change?
- Can you provide the increase calculation in writing?
- If the landlord expects your agreement, what happens if you do not consent?
- Are there any renewal or termination deadlines connected to the lease end date?
- Can you confirm whether any other terms change besides the rent amount?

## Polite Email Draft Requesting Clarification

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/phone.svg

Subject: Request for clarification on proposed rent increase and notice timing

Dear [Landlord’s Name],

I hope you are well. I am writing regarding the proposed **12% rent increase** and the clause in the lease referring to **3 months’ notice**.

Could you please clarify:
- the exact lease clause or basis for the proposed increase,
- the date from which the higher rent would apply,
- whether the 3-month notice clause relates to rent changes, lease termination, or renewal, and
- how the increase has been calculated?

For reference, my current lease ends on **2026-08-31**, so I would appreciate confirmation of how this relates to the proposed timing.

Thank you for your help. I would be grateful if you could send the details in writing so I can review them properly.

Kind regards,
[Your Name]
[Apartment Address]
[Phone Number]
